name: Master of Social Work (Qualifying)
description: A qualifying degree for graduates of another field who want to practise as social workers. You learn to assess a person's situation, plan support with them and work within child protection, mental health and justice systems. Two long field placements, supervised by a qualified social worker, are part of the course.

name: Master of Social Work (Qualifying)
description: Built around case work, this course has you practise interviews, risk assessments and case notes in small groups before you meet clients on placement. Units on trauma, disability and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander perspectives shape how you work with people in hospitals, councils and community agencies.
units: Working with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Communities

name: Master of Social Work (Qualifying)
description: How do families, laws and services shape a person's life, and where can a social worker step in? Teaching combines seminars on policy and research with skills workshops, and you complete supervised placements in settings such as hospitals, family services and housing.

name: Master of Social Work (Qualifying)
description: Small classes in Hobart and a focus on rural and regional practice, where one social worker often covers many roles. You learn community development alongside case work and crisis response. Placements may take you into smaller towns as well as the city.

name: Diploma of Community Services
description: Trains case workers and support workers for community organisations. You learn to work with people facing hardship, coordinate services around them and keep clear records, with a work placement in a community service during the year.
